content.rendered:
Pure Vet is a newly established independent veterinary practice based in Ashford. The client approached TDC following previous experience delivering veterinary practice design and fit-out projects, seeking a complete end-to-end solution for their new facility.

The brief was for TDC to design and deliver a full veterinary practice fit out, ensuring the space was not only functional and efficient for clinical use but also fully compliant with all relevant Building Regulations and Veterinary good practice standards.

TDC developed initial layout plans based on the client’s requirements, refining the design to improve workflow, operational efficiency, and overall usability. A key focus was ensuring the practice layout supported smooth day-to-day operations while meeting strict regulatory standards.

To support approval, we produced and coordinated all necessary compliance documentation, including:

  • Fire strategy
  • Accessibility regulations
  • Energy assessments
  • Full Building Regulations submission package

These submissions were prepared and presented to Building Control to secure Building Regulations approval at an early stage of the project.

As part of the wider scope, TDC also designed and coordinated all core building services, including:

  • HVAC (heating, ventilation and air conditioning) systems
  • Electrical infrastructure and distribution
  • Fire detection systems
  • Plumbing and drainage layouts
  • Internal finishes, including flooring, painting, and reception areas

Each element was carefully integrated to ensure the building operated efficiently and met the specific requirements of a modern veterinary practice.

Early collaboration with the landlord played a key role in the success of the project, enabling strategic installation of foul drainage in optimal locations, coordination and confirmation of adequate power capacity, and support with elements of the base building structure where required. This proactive approach helped avoid costly redesigns and ensured the building infrastructure fully supported the proposed clinical layout.

Sustainability was also considered throughout the design process. Energy-efficient solutions were incorporated wherever possible, including the use of a heat pump hot water system to help reduce ongoing energy consumption and improve long-term efficiency.

The project was successfully delivered on time and within budget, providing Pure Vet with a fully operational, compliant, and modern veterinary practice ready for immediate opening.

The result? A well-planned clinical environment that supports both staff efficiency and patient care, while meeting all regulatory and technical requirements from the outset.

content.rendered:
Tim Day Construction delivered a traditionally styled, brick and block-built detached home using a cavity wall system for reliable thermal and structural performance.

While the superstructure followed a standard approach, the foundations for this project utilised a piled raft foundation using the specialist Housedeck solution. This involves a patented piled raft foundation and ground floor solution designed for residential structures. 

This piled foundation system was implemented with the main structure in mind, as structural slabs are suspended on piles with a void beneath to prevent issues caused by soil movement.

Housedeck offers cost and programme certainty, performing up to 70% faster than traditional methods, while also being safer (LABC and NHBC approved) and more environmentally friendly by reducing concrete use, spoil removal, and site traffic. 

It replaces the need for strip or pile-and-beam foundations and suits all construction types, including timber frame and modular builds, with adaptability for varied ground conditions, heave risks or potential gas presence.

This combination of classic building methods and modern engineering showcases Tim Day Construction’s ability to adapt and deliver high-quality results on more complex residential projects.

From concept to completion, this project demonstrates our commitment to delivering bespoke, high-quality new builds with structural integrity and premium design.

This 8-bed, 6-bathroom property lies along the coast in Whitstable and was designed to embrace the seaside views. TDC created an unparalleled Rooftop Experience for the client with a far reaching view over Whitstable.

External blockwork cavity walls were finished with a thin, Baumit coat render for a sleek, high-quality finish whilst the front façade was built with a full-height aluminium curtain wall to enhance the natural light and modern aesthetics.

With both sustainability and design in mind, aluminium double-glazed windows were installed throughout the home to ensure energy efficiency whilst giving a contemporary look. The tall ceilings create an open, airy feel, enhancing the overall sense of space.

For superior durability, strength and sound reduction, the property was built with bison precast hollow core concrete floors across the first and second levels, whilst the ground floor is fully tiled for aesthetics. All three floors have precast concrete stairs and underfloor heating within sand/cement screed, providing efficient and discreet warmth. 

With a 10-Year NHBC Warranty, this property is built to the highest standards, ensuring long-term durability, efficiency, and peace of mind for its occupants.

Having recently acquired architectural drawings, the client asked us to take charge of the project, managing all consultants and ensuring adherence to critical regulations and compliance, including accessibility, fire safety, and building control standards.

TDC exceeded expectations by fully insulating the structure to meet new-build standards. This enhanced thermal performance elevated the building’s Energy Performance Certificate rating.

A new heating and ventilation system was installed, ensuring a comfortable environment for both the veterinary team and their animal patients.

Rachel, Private Client

“We would highly recommend Tim Day Construction for any commercial building work. Tim, Barry and the whole team were professional and reliable. We had a very clear vision of how we wanted our veterinary practice to look and feel and they really listened to what we wanted and enabled our vision to become reality both on budget and within the expected timescale. They were on board with us from start to finish and fully understood the project inside out. They are also really nice people to work with and I never felt that any questions, however silly were too much trouble for them.

We could not be happier with the end result and would highly recommend Tim Day Construction to anyone contemplating a commercial project.”

content.rendered:
The South Foreland Lighthouse was the first lighthouse ever to shine an electric light and was acquired by the National Trust in 1989. Due to it’s historic character, Tim Day Construction were appointed by The National Trust to carefully manage this project.

Tim Day Construction conducted a complete interior refurbishment of the lighthouse which included the removal of moisture-damaged plaster from the inner walls, as well as removing multiple layers of modern impervious paint. A dehumidifier was then installed to maintain the humidity inside the tower at around 60%. After a year long drying process, the walls were coated with 3 layers of bespoke lime plaster (to match the lighthouse’s original composition) before re-painting with a breathable paint.
 
The lighthouse was discreetly re-wired, allowing original cabling to remain due to it’s historical importance. Additional curved glass balustrades were also added around the optics for aesthetic appeal, whilst enhancing safety and visitor access.

Since the refurbishment, Tim Day Construction have twice been awarded the contract to paint the whole structure externally over the years.

Heritage properties like the South Foreland Lighthouse hold significant historical, architectural, and cultural value. Restoring them helps preserve the tangible links to our past, ensuring that future generations can appreciate and learn from their rich history.

Mr N, The National Trust

“I think it only right that at this point I record and minute our gratitude to Tim Day and all his team for their diligent work during all phases of this contract and the impressive results that they have achieved.

Few other contractors I work with work in such a helpful and collaborative manner which has been so helpful in this case and achieved excellent results. Thank you.“

King Post in Elham is 400 years old and was formerly a house and shop. The building from the late 15th century is on the National Heritage List for England, which is a unique register of our country’s most significant historic buildings and sites.

The Grade II listed building has been continuously refurbished in its time, in line with every significant architectural fashion from its origin.

Tim Day Construction were trusted to maintain the conservation of this cherished historical building by giving it a general refurbishment. TDC carried out various repairs, decorated the interior and gave the electrical works a re-fresh.

content.rendered:
When a local client sought to add more accommodation and modernise their beachfront property, while embracing the stunning views of the Thames Estuary, Tim Day Construction delivered a clever and stylish solution.

By creating an “upside-down” layout with bedrooms situated on the ground floor and living spaces on the first, the home now maximises the beautiful sunset views from all areas of the property. The living spaces on the top floor overlook and sea views, while the main bedroom below is fitted with en-suite facilities, and a decked terrace overlooking the seafront.

This coastal property is now let weekly as an elegant holiday home.

If your current residence no longer accommodates your needs, but you have an attachment to your current location or want to avoid the complexities of constructing a new home elsewhere, an extension could be the ideal solution for you.

Andy Boorman, Private Client

“It was important for me as a local Whitstable resident to use a local builder, and I am very happy I did!

During this project, Tim Day’s team demonstrated exceptional professionalism, expertise and dedication.

Their attention to detail, quality workmanship and commitment to meeting deadlines were impressive.”

Inside, there are three reception rooms, one with a part-vaulted ceiling and two sets of French doors, overlooking and opening onto the gardens. The kitchen is fitted with a range of ‘Integra Soho’ units, completed by polished granite worksurfaces and a statement central island.

The staircase rises to the partially galleried first floor landing, which centres the five bedrooms, all of which are equipped with ensuites featuring automatic lighting and high-quality fittings and tiling.

Modern systems elevate the home’s comfort and efficiency, including a 16kW Samsung EHS Monobloc heat pump and energy-saving LED lighting. Security and convenience are prioritised with remote-controlled solid timber gates, a video intercom, and a permeable brick-paved driveway. New Builds are designed with the latest in energy-saving technologies and building materials, which leads to reduced utility bills and a smaller carbon footprint, while also complying with modern building standards.

The house has a NHBC Buildmark warranty with impressive specifications and meticulous detail. Every element of the project was thoughtfully planned, making it a standout property in every way.

content.rendered:
This impressive looking seafront property was designed and forged around the clients’ desire to have large open plan living spaces on multiple levels. 

The front lounge boasts large bifold doors and fixed glazing which make the most of the impressive views and sunsets over Whitstable Bay.

The property’s structural elements comprise of a Douglas Fir timber structural frame, with a white softwood finish, which was infilled with Structurally Insulated Panels. These were then clad externally in Canadian ‘Cape Cod’ pre painted cladding to give that desired ‘beach house effect’.

There are many benefits to using a timber frame for new builds including sustainability, design flexibility, speed of construction, longevity and durability.

Another benefit of using timber frames is energy efficiency. Timber frames excel in thermal performance and allow for high levels of insulation, keeping homes warm in winter and cool in summer. To no surprise, this house was designed to Code 4 of the code for sustainable homes and thus highly energy efficient.

content.rendered:
After purchasing this historic dwelling, unoccupied for 2 years, the clients decided it was the perfect time for a complete transformation; double the buildings size with a large extension, whilst preserving its cherished original features.

The property underwent a full remodel, including new structural and insulated slab flooring with underfloor heating across both the first and second floors. Tim Day Construction built a two-sided fireplace with a traditional brick chimney breast to feature in the open plan living area.

The roof was reconfigured with eco-friendly Steicoflex wood fiber insulation (an eco-friendlier version of traditional roof insulation), and sustainability is further embraced with solar panels and an air source heat pump.

Many homeowners prefer to preserve the character and heritage of their current homes by renovating or extending them, rather than starting anew. This 30-week project is a perfect example of how extension projects can be utilised to adjust a property, specific to a client’s needs, whilst maintaining its historical charm.
